source: M. Jutila On Linnik's constant Math Scand 41 (1977) theorem 1 eq (1.8) is PRIMITIVE summed over q<=Q, not all characters
exact_induction_count_identity: S_all(Q)=sum_d<=Q floor(Q/d)*a_d = sum_k<=Q A_prim(floor(Q/k)); a_d primitive zero-count at conductor d
upper_bound_deduction: If A_prim(U) <= C*(U^2*T)^a with a=(2+eps)(1-alpha), then S_all(Q) <= C*(Q^2*T)^a*sum_{k<=Q}k^(-2a). For 2a<1 this is O(C*Q*T^a), not O(C*Q^(2a)*T^a) without other input. For 2a=1 add logQ; for 2a>1 no power loss.
qualification: The single conductor toy assigns a fictitious zero; it is an exact combinatorial countermodel to an illegitimate inference, not a statement that real Dirichlet characters have zeros off critical line. Source eq(1.7) separately bounds all characters for ONE fixed modulus q; check whether the archive uses (1.7) or (1.8) before drawing any conclusion about source fidelity.
